notes: Summary: Emberline evaluating Redwood Dedicated for mission-critical inference across fleet management and operator assistance.

Primary asks: throughput guarantees for sustained 400 reqs/sec across 6 regional pools; 50ms median tail latency target for operator-assist chat; predictable reserved GPU planning (initial 20x A100-equivalent), burst to 40x during release windows.

SLA negotiation focus: customer pushing for 99.995% uptime SLA or compensatory credit schedule that scales (financial credits + priority support) — they called out 4.38 minutes/month downtime budget for critical services.
Credit schedule requested by Emberline: sliding scale starting at 5% monthly credit for <99.99%, 20% for <99.9%, escalate for repeated misses. Legal flagged for Redwood review.

Maintenance windows: Emberline requires maintenance to be pre-scheduled with minimum 30-day notice for non-emergency work; emergency maintenance allowed only with on-call approval and compensating credits if >15 minutes impact.
Support / escalation: P1 response target 15 minutes, P2 2 hours, P3 24 hours. They want named on-call escalation contacts and monthly SLA reports with token-level latency histograms.

Security & compliance: must meet ISO27001 evidence, SOC2 Type II in progress acceptable, on-prem control plane option for PRD fleet — KMS integration mandatory, logs forwarded to customer SIEM and 13-month retention.

POC notes: 6-week POC scoped — week1 infra prep, week2 model onboarding, week3 latency tuning and kernel selection, week4 loadgen + KV cache validation, week5 failover and routing test, week6 SLA measurement run.
Quotes/voice-of-customer: "We can tolerate bursts, but sustained tail latency kills operator trust. Uptime math must be unambiguous in the contract." — Head of Operations (A. Keller)
Financials: procurement comfortable with ARR band but needs firm SLOs to include in capital approval packet.
Technical concerns raised by SE: how Redwood's autoscaling interacts with reserved capacity and burst pools; need deterministic routing policy for latency-sensitive traffic.
Action items assigned: SE to produce reserved GPU sizing doc + sequence-of-failure playbook; AE to coordinate legal exchange; Solutions to produce sample SLA credit table by 2026-03-17.
Risk: If Redwood cannot commit to maintenance restrictions and credit terms, Emberline will re-engage competitor proof-of-concept in parallel (ModelHoster currently running initial sizing).
